description: Single-DGX-Spark Qwen3.8 Flash Next on Ash Hart's TensorFold engine v0.6.6 (exact decoding, custom CUDA kernels JIT-compiled on first start, stock upstream source) with local-inference-lab's quantization-aware-distilled NVFP4 checkpoint (NVFP4 routed experts and n-gram tables, MXFP8 attention, DeltaNet and shared experts, MTP head included; about 98.6 GiB), which TensorFold's CUDA engine reads as it ships on one GPU. Chosen over RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 (about 126 GiB, bf16 besides the experts), which does not fit 128 GB. The n-gram tables stay memory-mapped from the checkpoint (upstream refuses --ple-on-ssd on NVFP4 checkpoints, since they already are), so page-cache pressure, not a flag, governs speed. Serves one request at a time by default (upstream CUDA default; the concurrency setting enables shared rounds) at the 262,144-token window with a bf16 KV cache. Text only here: TensorFold adds Flash Next image input on CUDA from 0.6.1 (video from 0.6.3, which needs PyAV, not installed), and this recipe does not expose it (the MLX 4-bit recipe qwen3-8-flash-next-tensorfold-single carries MiaAI-Lab's vision patch). Upstream publishes no speed or memory figure for this checkpoint on a Spark, and none is measured here; the memory envelope below is the checkpoint size plus KV. The model weights are under the Qwen Community License 1.0 (attribution above 100M MAU or US$20M monthly revenue; separate licence for Model-as-a-Service or AI Work Assistant businesses); TensorFold is Apache-2.0 from 0.6.0 (MIT up to 0.5.0). TensorFold v0.6.6 at cb2ebf0540f42604e2759b2ddef497861e928248, the newest release of TensorFold's Python engine line (0.6; TensorFold 1.x is a native binary that serves only Nemotron on CUDA), keeps every option this recipe passes. Per upstream's release notes it runs CUDA prompts at bf16 by default and serves Prometheus /metrics, fills prompts inside the decode rounds when concurrency is above 1, resumes resends on Flash Next, and decodes NVFP4 checkpoints 4.9-7.1% faster with 15-16% faster prompt fill (upstream claims, unmeasured here); the existing context bound, KV/drafting defaults, and one-stream resource profile are retained. From 0.6.1 to 0.6.6 upstream's release notes add, among others, the Anthropic Messages API (/v1/messages), optional API keys (not set here), /v1/decisions scoring and joint prefill of prompts that wait together when concurrency is above 1. 0.6.4 refuses GPUs below sm_120 at startup (the Spark's GB10 is sm_121). The pinned ARM64 image includes xgrammar 0.2.8 and Apache TVM FFI 0.1.11 for OpenAI response_format structured-output requests. Thinking is chosen per request (chat template kwargs or sampling parameters), not as a recipe option; server default: Open a think block by default (upstream default: --thinking).
title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next NVFP4 TensorFold single Spark
